editorial:
Imagine getting a backstage pass to the raw, unfiltered world of French rap during its peak. You get to follow the legendary duo Kool Shen and Joeystarr for a whole year, seeing everything from their gritty studio sessions in Aubervilliers to their massive tour across cities like Lyon and Bordeaux. The vibe is very personal and honest. You aren't just watching a concert movie; you are seeing the stress, the fights with the media, and the legal headaches that come with being famous rebels. It feels like you are hanging out with the group, watching their friendship be tested while they try to stay true to their roots.

What really makes this work is the way the interviews are mixed in with the tour footage. You see the chaos of the road and then hear the guys reflect on it with a lot of maturity. The pacing is steady and keeps you interested because it balances the high energy of the Zénith in Paris with quiet, real moments. If you love music history or just want to see how a rap empire is run, you need to see this.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up as the group reaches their huge show at the Zénith in Paris. After all the travel and drama, you see them reflect on whether NTM can keep going. They talk about their new projects like B.O.S.S. and IV My People. Instead of a happy ending, it ends on a thoughtful note about their legacy and the possibility that the group might eventually come to an end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves hip hop history and behind the scenes music stories.
